newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan supermarkets competitive, quality varies-S&P.
newsitem.headline: Japan supermarkets competitive, quality varies-S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Thursday that Japanese supermarket chain operators were competitive compared with other retailers but that the credit quality among the six largest operators varied greatly.
Improving efficiency will be crucial for success in the industry, where competition is intensifying, S&P said.
The six largest operators are Ito-Yokado Co Ltd, Uny Co Ltd, Daiei Inc, Jusco Co Ltd, Mycal Corp and Seiyu Ltd.
The business profiles of Ito-Yokado, Uny and Jusco were rated above average or well above average, while Daiei and Mycal were considered average and Seiyu below average, S&P said.
The six firms are engaged in a wide range of retailing activities, including convenience stores, supermarkets and department stores, as well as non-retailing activities.
S&P said the overall business profiles of Japan's supermarket chain operators, which have rapidly taken on an important role in the retail sector, were above average by international standards.
They benefit from low cyclicality, advantageous locations for their outlets and barriers to entry, S&P said.
It added that supermarket operators are currently in a difficult environment, however, because of weak consumption and increasing competition.

Prospects for a recovery in Japanese consumer spending in 1997 remain limited given the sluggish economy, the consumption tax increase in April and the termination of special income tax reductions, the rating agency said.
